author: Bobby Grayson
description:
Things found while building the local-function facility that a sibling or the integrator will hit.

1) A tagged union with exactly one alternative is not recognised. A file whose only reply literal is {:size, n} infers @type reply :: {:size, term()}, and lean_type/3 then fails with "unsupported type {:size, term()}" because a bare tuple type is only allowed at state level. Two alternatives work. This is pre-existing (untyped mode, infer_types/2), not something this branch introduced; worth a fix in the union-building code, which this branch does not own.

2) An unused `fresh` binder trips Lean's linter. A clause whose only spawn binds its pid to an unused variable ("{:ok, _p} = GenServer.start_link(..)") still renders the second beh binder as `fresh`, and Lean reports "Variable name `fresh` is not explicitly referenced" -- a warning, so check.sh fails. fresh_name/1 keys off :__fresh__ being in the env rather than off the pid actually being used. Worked around in the init_stmts fixture by using the pid.

3) A local binding whose right-hand side type is unknown gets no env entry. In a helper body, "let x := ..." with an untypable right-hand side leaves x untyped, so a later use of x at a typed position renders without the conversion. It does not misrender today (Lean infers the let), but a case scrutinee over such an x fails with "untyped scrutinee".

4) `[k | l]` is not an expression form. List cons is supported in patterns but not in expressions, so a handler that prepends has to write "l ++ [k]". Cheap to add, in the expression builder's area.

5) Elixir parses "def foo do .. end" with args = nil, not []. Both local_defs/2 in the translator and in the harness normalise with "args || []" so a zero-arity helper is found; a bare "foo" without parentheses is still a variable reference as far as the AST goes and is not rewritten to a call.

6) A pipe hides a local call's arity. "socket |> reload_prs()" is the node reload_prs/0, so the harness labels it an imported/macro call even though reload_prs/1 is defined in the module. That is why the "call to an imported function or macro" family barely moved (156 -> 155): most of it is genuine Phoenix imports (assign/2 and assign/3 are 123 of the 155), and the rest is this pipe artefact, which the pipe feature will absorb.
title: Translator limits found while building local functions
